records.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure
records.description: The B58 engine's high-pressure fuel pump can fail, though at lower rates than the older N54 engine. When the HPFP fails, fuel pressure drops below the minimum required for proper direct injection, causing long cranking, rough idle, misfires, and in severe cases, the engine stalling and entering limp mode. Failures are more common in cold weather when fuel demands are higher, and can be exacerbated by ethanol-blended fuels.
records.solution: Replace the high-pressure fuel pump with the latest revised BMW part number. Verify the low-pressure fuel pump is providing adequate feed pressure. Use top-tier fuel and avoid running the tank below 1/4 to reduce strain on the fuel system. If under warranty, BMW will cover HPFP replacement.
symptoms: Long cranking before engine starts, especially in cold weather
Engine stalling at idle or low speed
Check engine light with fuel pressure codes
Noticeable loss of power during acceleration
Rough idle and misfires

citations.title: Bimmerpost G20 - M340i Common Issues Before Buying

communityRecommendations.content: Log fuel pressure data with an OBD scanner like the BimmerLink app. Fuel pressure below 150 bar at full load is a sign the HPFP is failing before you get a check engine light.
The B58 HPFP is significantly more reliable than the N54's notorious pump. Most B58 HPFP failures occur on tuned cars - stock cars rarely have this issue before 80k miles.

records.title: 12V Battery Drain and Failure / Battery Registration Issues
records.description: M340i owners report the 12V AGM battery discharging or dying, sometimes on relatively young cars, often triggered by short-trip driving, parasitic drains from modules not entering sleep mode, or a failing Intelligent Battery Sensor (IBS). German owners on motor-talk specifically flag early failures of the OEM Sebang battery. After any DIY battery swap, failing to register the new battery to the power-management system leads to undercharging and repeat failures, and can leave a black iDrive screen plus multiple warning messages after a disconnect.
records.solution: Test and replace the AGM battery with the correct OEM-spec unit, then register the new battery with BimmerLink/ISTA so the charging strategy adapts. Diagnose parasitic drain and a faulty IBS cable/sensor if discharge persists. Drive long enough to fully recharge between trips.
symptoms: Dead or weak battery, hard / no start
Increased battery discharge warning
Multiple warning messages or black iDrive screen after battery disconnect
Electrical glitches after short trips

records.title: Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
records.description: As a direct-injection engine, the B58 in the M340i does not have fuel washing over the intake valves, leading to gradual carbon deposit buildup on the valve backs. Oil vapors from the crankcase ventilation system deposit carbon that restricts airflow and reduces performance. Symptoms typically become noticeable after 50,000-80,000 miles, with rough idle, reduced throttle response, and minor misfires. The M340i's higher boost pressures can accelerate carbon accumulation compared to non-M B58 applications.
records.solution: Walnut blast the intake valves every 50,000-60,000 miles. This involves removing the intake manifold and blasting walnut shell media at the valve backs to remove carbon deposits. Some owners use catch cans to reduce oil vapor entering the intake. BMW's official position is that carbon buildup is normal for direct-injection engines.
symptoms: Rough or uneven idle developing gradually
Reduced throttle response and power
Slight hesitation during acceleration from low RPM
Minor misfires at idle, especially when cold
Decreased fuel economy over time

citations.title: Adelaide Auto Pro - BMW M340i Common Problems: Carbon Buildup

communityRecommendations.content: Schedule a walnut blast at 50k miles as preventive maintenance. It costs $400-600 at an independent BMW shop and makes a huge difference in how the engine runs.

An oil catch can from Burger Motorsports or Mishimoto can significantly reduce carbon buildup by catching oil vapors before they enter the intake. Not a complete solution but helps extend time between walnut blasts.

records.title: Coolant Loss from Expansion Tank and Water Pump
records.description: The M340i's B58 engine experiences the same coolant loss issues as other B58-powered BMWs, but the M340i's higher sustained performance driving tends to accelerate the problem. The plastic coolant expansion tank develops hairline cracks from heat cycling, and the electric water pump can fail prematurely. BMW issued a TSB for the coolant vent line on the cylinder head that deteriorates under high temperatures. Many M340i owners report needing to top off coolant more frequently than expected, even on low-mileage vehicles.
records.solution: Replace the coolant expansion tank at first sign of cracking. Proactively replace the electric water pump before 60,000 miles. Replace the coolant vent line per BMW TSB. Use only BMW-approved blue coolant. Monitor coolant level monthly and pressure test the cooling system at every major service.
symptoms: Coolant level dropping between services
Low coolant warning on iDrive
Sweet antifreeze smell from engine compartment
Visible coolant residue or white deposits around expansion tank
Engine temperature gauge reading higher than normal
Steam from engine bay in severe cases

citations.title: BMW TSB - Replace Coolant Vent Line on Cylinder Head
Bimmerpost G20 - B58 Coolant Loss Thread

communityRecommendations.content: The B58 can go from 'low coolant' to 'overheated' very quickly. If you see the warning, pull over immediately. Driving even 5 minutes with overheating can warp the aluminum head.
FCP Euro carries the OEM Mahle water pump with their lifetime replacement guarantee. Worth every penny for this known failure item.

records.title: Oil Filter Disintegration in Housing
records.description: The B58 engine has a documented tendency for paper oil filters to shred and break apart during normal use. As oil passes through the filter under pressure, the filter media can separate from the end caps and tear into multiple pieces. Shredded filter material can deposit paper fragments in the oil filter housing and potentially circulate through the oil system. This is more common with non-OEM filters but has been reported with genuine BMW filters as well.
records.solution: Use only genuine BMW or Mann-branded oil filters (Mann is the OEM supplier). Change oil and filter every 5,000-7,000 miles rather than BMW's recommended 10,000-mile interval. When removing the old filter, inspect it carefully for signs of deterioration. If filter fragments are found in the housing, flush the housing thoroughly before installing the new filter.
symptoms: Oil filter found shredded or torn during oil change
Paper debris visible in oil filter housing
Low oil pressure warning (if fragments restrict flow)
Oil appearing darker than expected between changes
Fine metal particles in oil (if unfiltered oil reaches bearings)

citations.title: SlashGear - Common Problems With BMW B58 Engines According To Owners

communityRecommendations.content: Never use cheap aftermarket oil filters on the B58. The OEM Mann filter is only $8-12 and specifically engineered for the pressure and flow characteristics of this engine.
Shorten your oil change interval to 5,000-7,000 miles regardless of what BMW's oil life monitor says. The 10,000-mile interval is too long for the B58, especially in performance driving.

records.title: Turbo Wastegate Rattle at Idle
records.description: The B58 engine's electronic wastegate actuator can develop play over time, producing a characteristic rattling or buzzing noise at idle and during deceleration. The wastegate flapper valve develops clearance within its housing, causing it to vibrate at certain RPMs. While often described as just an annoyance, a severely worn wastegate can lead to boost control issues, over-boost or under-boost conditions, and eventually check engine lights for boost deviation faults.
records.solution: Have the wastegate actuator inspected for excessive play. Minor rattle without fault codes can be monitored. If boost control faults develop, replace the turbocharger wastegate actuator. In severe cases, the entire turbocharger assembly may need replacement. BMW may cover under warranty if fault codes are present.
symptoms: Rattling or buzzing noise at idle from turbocharger area
Metallic vibration sound during deceleration
Check engine light with boost control codes (advanced cases)
Intermittent boost fluctuations at steady throttle
Noise more pronounced in cold weather

citations.title: Oriona2 - BMW M340i Common Problems: Wastegate Rattle

communityRecommendations.content: A minor wastegate rattle without any codes is cosmetic - many B58 owners live with it for years without issues. Only worry if you get boost-related fault codes.

records.title: Loss of Brake Assist from Brake Vacuum Pump Damage (Recall 21V-598)
records.description: Faulty engine management software (DME) can command the combined oil/vacuum pump that supplies vacuum for power brake boost in a way that damages it under certain engine-start conditions — for example pressing the start/stop button twice in quick succession, or tapping the brake pedal very briefly while pressing start. A damaged vacuum pump reduces or eliminates brake assist (boost), so the pedal becomes very hard and braking distances increase, though full mechanical braking is retained. NHTSA campaign 21V-598 covers roughly 10,877 M340i / M340i xDrive units built for the 2020 model year.
records.solution: Free dealer remedy under recall 21V-598: reprogram the engine control units (DME) with corrected software. If the vacuum/oil pump was already damaged before the software fix, it must be replaced. Owners can check the recall by VIN at nhtsa.gov; notification letters were mailed September 2021.
symptoms: Hard, stiff brake pedal requiring much more force
Increased stopping distances
Reduced or absent brake boost after certain start sequences
Brake warning message

citations.title: The Recall Notice Looks Under the Hood at BMW Recall 21V598 - Sibros

records.title: Seat Belt Warning Audio Failure (Recall, RAM Software)
records.description: On certain 2019-2022 M340i vehicles, a software defect in the receiver audio module (RAM) control unit can prevent the car from generating the audible seat belt reminder chime for the driver. Without the audible warning, an unbelted driver may be less likely to buckle up, which fails to meet FMVSS 208 occupant-protection requirements and increases injury risk in a crash.
records.solution: Free dealer remedy under the NHTSA recall: reprogram/update the receiver audio module (RAM) control unit software. Check eligibility by VIN at nhtsa.gov; owner notification letters were mailed October 2023.
symptoms: No audible seat belt warning chime when driver unbelted
Recall notice received from BMW

records.title: Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gasket Oil Leaks (B58)
records.description: The rubber valve-cover gasket and the oil filter housing gasket on the B58 inline-six harden and crack from repeated heat cycling, allowing engine oil to seep out. It typically appears from roughly 60,000-100,000 miles. Leaking oil can drip onto hot exhaust components (burning smell) and pool in the spark-plug wells, eventually fouling coils/plugs and causing misfires if left unaddressed.
records.solution: Replace the valve cover gasket and/or oil filter housing gasket. Many shops also replace the valve cover itself if it has warped. Clean any oil from spark-plug wells and inspect coils. Typical independent-shop cost is roughly $400-$900 depending on which gasket(s) and labor access.
symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay
Oil staining around top of engine
Oily/soaked spark plug wells
Gradual drop in oil level
Misfire if oil contaminates coils

records.title: VANOS Solenoid O-Ring Failure
records.description: The B58 uses VANOS (variable valve timing) solenoids whose internal rubber O-rings degrade from heat and oil contamination, and the solenoid electronics can fail over time. A leaking O-ring lets oil pass where it should not and disrupts cam-timing control, producing rough running, hesitation, and in some cases limp mode. It is a common B58 wear item rather than a catastrophic failure.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool (VANOS/camshaft position fault codes), then replace the affected intake/exhaust VANOS solenoid(s) and O-rings. Solenoids are relatively inexpensive parts; cost is mostly diagnosis and labor, typically a few hundred dollars.
symptoms: Rough idle
Hesitation / sluggish acceleration
Reduced fuel economy
Limp mode in some cases
Check engine light

records.title: ZF 8HP Harsh / Jerky Low-Speed Shifting and Mechatronic Faults
records.description: Owners report harsh or jerky shifts from the ZF 8-speed automatic, most noticeable on the 1-2 and 2-3 changes at low speed before the drivetrain is warmed up, and aggravated by Sport mode in cold stop-and-go traffic. The ZF 8HP is sensitive to fluid condition; degraded or low fluid worsens shift quality, and in more severe cases the mechatronic valve body/control unit develops faults causing erratic shifting and transmission warning lights.
records.solution: Perform the ZF 8-speed fluid-and-filter (pan) service rather than treating it as lifetime-fill; this resolves many shift-quality complaints. Let the drivetrain warm before hard driving. For persistent erratic shifting or warning lights, scan the transmission and repair/replace the mechatronic unit (valve body) as needed.
symptoms: Jerky 1-2 / 2-3 shifts when cold
Harsh engagement at low speed
Delayed or erratic shifting
Transmission warning light
